summary: A fast, tight two-player skirmish game where you summon units from a hand of cards onto a small grid, attack with dice, and race to kill the enemy summoner before they kill yours. Games run 30-45 minutes once you know the factions, with constant back-and-forth tempo swings and a strong deckbuilding/faction-identity layer on top.
praised: Extremely fast setup and short, tense playtime
Strong asymmetric faction design where each army feels distinct to play
Good depth-to-complexity ratio for a card/dice combat game
High production quality and faction expandability in the 2nd edition relaunch
Tactical positioning on the small grid matters a lot despite the simple ruleset
criticised: Dice-based combat introduces swingy randomness that can decide fights
Only 2 players, so it's a pure head-to-head confrontation game with no diplomacy or team play
Faction/card balance has been an ongoing point of debate across factions and expansions
Deck construction and faction knowledge create a real experience gap between new and veteran players

interaction.kind: direct open conflict and area denial on a shared grid

scoring.why: The game ends the instant one player's summoner is destroyed, so there is no point-counting at all.
